title: Dashboard sunsetting and trace tiering playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a pragmatic lifecycle and sunsetting policy for dashboards and trace retention tiers. It is intended to reduce telemetry cost, limit alert fatigue, and keep the operator surface focused on high-signal widgets while preserving the ability to investigate regressions.

Background / Motivation:
- Over time dashboards accumulate tiles and panels that are rarely used, produce noisy alerts, or duplicate other views. Left unchecked this increases query costs and makes oncall investigation slower.
- Trace retention is a major line item if we store high-resolution spans for long periods. We need principled tiers so operators can request longer retention for investigations without blowing the telemetry budget.

Definitions (short):
- Active dashboard: owner assigned, > 1 monthly visits by operator or product stakeholder, and at least one alert tied to a validated SLI.
- Idle dashboard: owner assigned but < 1 monthly visits OR panels with > 90% zero-result queries across the previous 30 days.
- Stale dashboard: no owner, < 1 visit/month, and not referenced in any runbook or playbook.
- Panel bloom: a panel that duplicates another panel within the same team surface (same query but different visualization).
- Trace tiers: Hot (30d full-span retention), Warm (90d sampled + metadata), Cold (365d aggregated traces/indices), Archive (on-demand retrieval from cold storage).

Dashboard lifecycle and triggers:
1) Proposal -> Draft: new dashboards must be submitted with a one-line objective, data cost estimate (approx query cost per week), owner, and at least one example investigation that uses it (sample queries).
2) Active -> Monitoring: dashboards in active state are reviewed quarterly for usage and alert precision. A lightweight template (owner, objective, SLIs used, link to runbook) must be maintained in the dashboard properties.
3) Idle -> Nudges: if usage < 1 visit/month or >50% of panels have stale queries for 30d, send automated nudge emails to owner (week 0) and Slack reminder to the team (week 1).
4) Stale -> Sunset candidate: after 30d of nudges with no action, dashboard is tagged as sunset-candidate and moved to the publicly visible 'Sunset queue' for 14 days.
5) Sunset -> Archive -> Delete: if no objection during the 14d window, dashboard is archived (read-only snapshot exported to storage and link saved) for 90 days then permanently deleted. Owners can request restoration within archive window (self-serve). Emergency hold: SRE/observability can halt deletion for 7d if the dashboard is being used in an incident.

Sunsetting signals (automated):
- Visit_count_30d < 1
- Panels_with_zero_results_ratio > 0.9 over 30d
- Query_cost_estimate_weekly > threshold AND N_users_using < 2
- No linked runbook or owner tag

Trace retention tiers and policy:
- Hot (default for newly onboarded model/service): 30 days of full spans including payload metadata and token-level spans. Used for fast postmortem and immediate regressions. Cost: approx X tokens-day (see cost calc below).
- Warm: 90 days of partial spans. Sampling policy (see below) preserves: 100% of traces for errors and alerts, 5% reservoir for high-volume success traces, and 100% for any trace with model-version change or quantization flag. This tier also keeps compact metadata for longer (inputs/outputs hashes, latency histograms).
- Cold: 365 days of aggregated trace indices + compact summaries (no raw spans). Full trace rehydration requires a cold-storage job (on-demand, 24–72h SLA).
- Archive: multi-year cryptographic store for compliance requests; retrieval is manual and expensive.

Sampling strategies (recommended defaults):
- Severity-weighted reservoir sampling: errors and alerts are sampled at 100%; success traces are sampled via reservoir with weight proportional to token_count and latency_outlier_score. Keep per-tenant caps for multi-tenant workloads.
- Session-aware retention: for multi-call sessions (chat chains), preserve full session traces when any call in the session triggers an error or anomaly.
- Prefix-key preservation: for KV cache investigations, keep first-n prefixes for 90% of traces in Warm tier to allow reconstruction of warm/cold-cache behavior.

Cost estimation example (quick heuristic):
- avg_span_size_bytes = 2.5KB
- spans_per_trace = 18 (typical multi-step chat)
- hot_daily_traces = 100k traces/day -> daily_raw_bytes = 100k * 18 * 2.5KB = ~4.5GB/day
- 30-day hot storage ~135GB -> multiply by replication + index overhead = multiply x3 -> ~405GB
- Use vendor storage pricing and index costs to convert to $/month. This explains why warm sampling for long horizons is necessary.

Dashboard rotation and operator rituals:
- Owners should rotate quarterly. Each owner provides a 15-minute 'dashboard health' update to the ops sync the week before rotation handoff.
- Oncall pairing: new owners and outgoing owners do a 1-hour walkthrough with annotated incident examples covering how the dashboard helped root cause (or failed). Add 2 'play' queries to exercise panels.
- Dashboard review checklist: objective exists, queries are parameterized (avoid hardcoded tenant ids), panels have SLA-backed alerts with runbook links, cost estimate present, and duplicate panels removed.

Automation checklist (observability infra):
- Daily job that tags panels meeting 'zero-result' criteria and annotates them with metrics (zero_ratio, last_query_ts, visit_count_30d).
- Weekly summary email to team Slack channel with 'top 10 sunset candidates' and per-dashboard cost delta if kept vs if archived.
- One-click archive export: JSON snapshot + SQL used + small visualization snapshot stored in archive bucket.

Runbook & incident integration:
- All production SLOs / SLIs must reference the dashboard tile used for the SLI, not the dashboard page. This allows detached tile ownership when sunsetting a page.
- When an incident references a dashboard slated for sunset, Incident Commander must mark it as 'critical' to pause sunset (automated).

Migration and deprecation notes for heavy-query panels:
- Replace heavy JOINs with precomputed materialized views updated on a cadence aligned with SLI resolution window (e.g., 1m or 5m).
- Introduce aggregated tiles with a hyperlink to a synthetic explorer that runs the heavy query on demand for deep investigation.

Owner-facing template (one-line, stored in dashboard properties):
- Objective: <one sentence>
- Primary SLI: <metric_name + threshold>
- Owner: <name + rotation quarter>
- Cost estimate: <$ / month or query-cost-tag>
- Runbook link: <confluence id>

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide strict cost threshold for automatic sunset vs manual review (proposal: >$500/mo for single dashboard with <2 users triggers engineering review).
- Define API for programmatic snapshot restore for archived dashboards (self-serve).
- Explore ML-based classifier to identify duplicate panels across teams (pilot Q2 2026).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- (Talia) Ship the nudge automation prototype to mark zero-result panels (2w).
- (Ethan) Run cost simulation for top-20 heavy dashboards and present numbers to SRE (1w).
- (Lucia) Draft owner template and add to dashboard creation flow (1w).
- (Ravi) Draft sample trace-sampling policy config examples for Hot/Warm tiers and upload to github:redwood/observability (2w).

Appendix: quick CLI queries (examples):
- visit_count_30d: SELECT dashboard_id, COUNT(*) FROM dashboard_access WHERE ts >= now() - 30d GROUP BY dashboard_id;
- panel_zero_ratio: SELECT panel_id, SUM(CASE WHEN results=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) as zero_ratio FROM panel_runs WHERE ts >= now() - 30d GROUP BY panel_id;

Contact: Talia Morgan (talia@redwood.ai) for clarifications and to request a temporary hold on a sunset candidate.

Notes: This doc is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is to reduce operator cognitive load and telemetry spend while preserving investigatory fidelity. Expect iterations after the first quarterly run of the automation.
